previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including end-stage renal disease, functioning pancreatic transplants, mechanical mitral valve, and peripheral vascular disease was admitted with fever and left lower extremity cellulitis, three days after noticing worsening redness and pain. She had a recent popliteal stent placement for a non-healing ulcer. On admission, she had a supratherapeutic INR of 10.1, which was corrected with vitamin K, and was started on a heparin drip. Blood cultures from the outside hospital grew Corynebacterium striatum, prompting treatment with IV vancomycin and levofloxacin. Imaging showed severe left-sided peripheral arterial disease with a necrotic left toe, and vascular surgery recommended amputation to prevent infection spread. The patient declined immediate surgery, opting to decide after discharge. Her infection improved clinically and laboratory markers trended favorably. She was discharged to extended care on a heparin drip, warfarin, IV vancomycin, and oral levofloxacin, with plans to follow up with her podiatrist regarding amputation.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ F w/ multiple medical issues including ___ pancreas/renal 
transplant, MWF HD(oliguric), MVR on coumadin, CHF with ICD, p/w 
syncope, anemia and a supratherapeutic INR. Hospital course is

#Acute on chronic anemia: Patient with baseline hgb ___, 
presenting with hgb of 5 in the setting of an INR of 15 at OSH. 
Possible sources include GI, as Patient had guiaic positive 
stool and melena during admission. Patient received a total of 
3U pRBC with appropriate rise in her Hb. GI was consulted for an 
EGD/colonoscopy which was performed on ___. This showed no 
single point of bleeding amenable to intervention. It was 
thought that her acute anemia was 2'/2 to her supratherapeutic 
INR leading to a diffuse but slow blood loss. She received 
another 2u pRBC the day before discharge given concern for a 
cardiac event (see below). Her Hb/HCT on dc were 9.1/29.0.   

#Syncope: Patient reports feeling dizzy prior to syncopizing, 
without CP or palpitations. Likely due to orthostatic 
hypotension vs acute on chronic anemia. Metoprolol was recently 
d/c'd ___ hypotension. Ddx also includes cardiac etiology, 
although patient with BiV pacemaker/ICD, last interrogated ___ 
with adequate battery life. Less likely neurologic, as patient 
describes dizziness, although somnelence on presentation could 
be post-ictal. Head CT negative. Patient had no further syncopal 
episodes during hospitalization.

# CAD ___ CABG, DES: continued patient's aspirin given 
significant cardiac history and stent placement. This was stable 
until 3 nights prior to discharge when the pt described a 
senstation of chest pressure with a troponinemia of 1.86 but a 
normal CK-MB 3. An EKG was concerning for TWI in II, III, and 
aVF. She was given aspirin and atorvastatin 80. Her INR at this 
point was 2.4. Cardiology was consulted and a stress test 
revealed only fixed defects that were previously known. 
Electrophysiology interrogated her device and found it to be 
functioning properly. It was likely that this troponinemia was 
not acute and was probably elevated in the context of demand 
ischemia from her anemia (Hb=5) several days before hand. It was 
the impression of cardiology that the pt did not suffer an acute 
cardiac event while in house.  

#End stage renal disease on HD: renal was c/s and patient 
continued HD during hospitalization on ___. She was maintained 
on her home regimen of nephrocaps, sevelamer, vitamin D.

#Hyperkalemia: 7.1 on presentation. Received insulin, calcium, 
and HD with appropriate normalization of K. Her K stayed below 
5.5 for the duration of her admission.

# ___ renal and pancreatic transplant: continued home prednisone 
5mg po daily, tacrolimus 2mg po q12h, and Bactrim ppx. 

# Supratherapeutic INR: 15 at OSH. Reversed with 10 mg Vit K. 
Has had prior admissions with elevated INR to 10. Unclear cause 
of supratherapeutic INR, dietary indiscretion vs recent 
antibiotic use. Once the patient's INR normalized, she was 
started on a heparin gtt. Over the course of her admission, she 
was successfully bridged from heparin to warfarin with her INR 
on discharge of 3.4. 

# Anion gap acidosis: Patient with anion gap of 23 on admission, 
likely secondary to BUN of 122. Initially also with elevated 
lactate, now normalized. Both her anion gap and acidosis 
normalized after volume resuscitation. 

# ___ mechanical MR replacement: held warfarin given 
supratherapeutic INR. Started heparin gtt once INR <2.5. She was 
then bridged to coumadin and was therapeutic with an INR of 3.4 
on discharge.

# chronic hand pain: continued patient's home tramadol. Patient 
reported that she takes morphine at home, however given mental 
status changes this was held on admission. Of note, patient was 
recently on prednisone 20 mg daily up from her baseline 5 mg 
daily to help with her hand pain (patient reports this was 
recommended by an ED physician). After discussion with her PCP, 
her steroid was decreased back to 5 mg daily. Given the severity 
of her pain she was given fentanyl boluses. She was evaluated by 
rheumatology for questionable scleroderma, but her hand pain and 
skin findings were thought to be 2'/2 chronic vascular disease 
rather than a primary rheumatological disorder. 

# Peripheral vascular disease, lower extremity ulcers: continued 
wound dressings to feet daily. Patient will f/u with vascular as 
an outpatient.
